A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison despite changed pagination and figure placement.

before.justification: v5 reports original recursive-training experiments with GPT-2 and SmolLM2, detector evaluations, and collapse-mitigation results in Tables 1–3 and S2.

after.justification: v6 retains original recursive-training, detector-performance, and mitigation results, including supplementary analyses across model sizes and data mixtures.

M1.justification: Recursive training, detector calibration, importance weights, 1.5-fold resampling, and the duplication cap remain unchanged. The shift from 'sampling' to 'resampling' and revised indices clarify the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both use WikiText-2 for text-generation experiments and MAGE, its out-of-distribution test set, and the RAID subset for detection. All model sizes, decoding scenarios, and human/synthetic mixtures were already represented in v5.

E2.justification: The six decoding strategies, RoBERTa/DeBERTav3/ModernBERT detector comparison, and unfiltered-training and Oracle comparators are retained. Table S2's 'sampling' becomes 'pure sampling' without changing comparator identity.

E3.justification: Splits, training budgets, metrics, decoding settings, and tested mixtures are retained. However, v6 Section 6.1 describes MAGE prompts as the first 30 words, whereas Appendix B.3 in both versions specifies 30 tokens. The conflicting descriptions leave the intended prompt specification unresolved; they do not establish rerunning experiments.

E4.justification: Model-size, mixing-condition, detector-score-distribution, and perplexity-distribution analyses already appear in v5. Combining v5 Figures 3 and S3 into v6 Figure 4 does not introduce a new analysis or robustness test.

E5.justification: Appendix B.2 retains detector-training seed 42. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance testing, and no uncertainty-reporting practice is added.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3, S1, and S2 retain their numerical values. Section 5 adds an approximately 2.5-fold deterministic-decoding perplexity increase and describes top-k as second-best in task performance. These revise result summaries; the unqualified multiplier conflicts with retained SmolLM2 greedy results, 13.96 to 85.69, approximately 6.1-fold.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 and the resampling formulation remain mathematically equivalent, with indexing changes. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and v6 adds none.

C1.justification: The abstract softens inevitable collapse from 'will' to 'could', while stating gains over human-only training without v5's sufficient-human-data proviso. The conclusion retains the equal-ratio condition. The central contributions and demonstrated model coverage remain the same.

C2.justification: v6 hypothesizes that lower-quality outputs explain smaller models' larger resampling gains. Its Limitations section replaces the explicit dependence on detector accuracy, bias, and robustness with a computational explanation for evaluating models below 2B parameters. The fine-tuning and task-generalization limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds licence disclosures for the three detector architectures, MAGE, and RAID. WikiText-2, GPT-2, and SmolLM2 licence information moves from the Ethics Statement into Appendix A. Hyperparameters and code/model access links are retained.

R1.justification: The introduction adds Wu et al. (2024) on self-improvement and Zhao et al. (2025) on reinforcement learning as controlled uses of synthetic data. Other publication and bibliography updates largely concern existing works; the central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v6 edits the abstract and explanatory paragraphs, standardizes resampling terminology, and corrects the reversed metric-based/neural-based detector descriptions in Section 4.4. It adds acknowledgments and removes the separate Ethics Statement, while retaining the main section structure.

P2.justification: v6 adds a recursive-training schematic, combines the GPT-2 and SmolLM2 perplexity distributions into Figure 4, and adjusts plot axes, captions, and appendix ordering. Tables retain their structure. The new Figure 2 incorrectly labels human-data arrows beta and current-synthetic-data arrows alpha, reversing Equation 3.

improvement.justification: The combined distribution display, corrected detector taxonomy, and additional disclosures improve exposition. However, v6 introduces reversed mixing labels in Figure 2 and an inaccurate general perplexity multiplier in Section 5, while removing the explicit detector-robustness limitation. These gains and losses affect both clarity and scientific accuracy, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
